script_findings.summary: TimeDilationEventsTransitions delegates activation to native TimeSystem.SetTimeDilation and local-player dilation; unsetting uses requested ease-out or None. Cleanup event may be queued immediately or delayed 1 second. No named VFX event or depot asset is provided here.

Sandevistan entry sets PSM TimeDilation=1, camera time-dilation curve Sandevistan, native global reason sandevistan; it clears competing kereznikov or existing sandevistan as shown. No StartEffectEvent call.
Forced exit, normal exit and photomode exit use native SandevistanEaseOut; photomode requests immediate cleanup. Normal exit updates timestamp/blackboard and removes Sandevistan-type statuses.
Native time dilation is reissued if the time-scale stat changes; manually starting replacement FX only on Bool activation is not proof of equivalent native lifecycle.
Kerenzikov uses separate kereznikov reason, camera curve Kerenzikov and slide/dodge ease-in, with KerenzikovEaseOut cleanup and separate status. The native key intentionally uses spelling kereznikov.
Player cleanup again calls native UnsetTimeDilation and local-player cleanup. IsRunning becoming false does not by itself prove all visual fade/exit work is finished.
TimeSystem Set/Unset methods are native declarations; actual VFX dispatch/renderer lifecycle is not available as a script method body.

tweak_findings.summary: The visible accepted reasons contain sandevistan for Sandy and kereznikov for Kerenzikov. The record contains no .effect/.particle/material/LUT paths or track inventory.
Player Sandevistan and cooldowned player variant definitions shown here do not enumerate a complete player screen effect asset graph.
TimeDilationStatusEffect parent defines tags/time-affect flags, not a screen-resource graph.
Kerenzikov player status config supplies gameplay data but not a complete screen-resource graph.

visualfix_1_0_0_fidelity_gaps.summary: Starts three private third-party-derived replacements and hard-stops selected native instances; cannot demonstrate preservation of all native tracks.
BreakEffectLoopEvent followed immediately by StopEffectEvent may cut a resource exit/loop-break tail. This is not proven equivalent to native ease-out/cleanup.
Requests end when strict activity becomes false, before proving native fade/exit completion; all replacements start together on Lua observation rather than native per-track triggers.
The ~0.76-second flash and its original third-party timing do not establish vanilla 2.5 startup timing; third-party resource names do not establish original provenance.

resource_paths.explicit_warning: This candidate path is present in the supplied third-party archive; its bytes and graph cannot be labelled vanilla. Actual installed vanilla archive must establish path/version and reference graph.

required_input: Original, unmodified 2.5 binary effect resource(s) actually referenced by the native player time-dilation FX component/system, exported from clean game archives (not from mod/archive overrides).

Their full dependency graph: referenced particle/material/curve/LUT/texture resources as present, preserving depot paths and embedded/external buffer data. Do not invent a fixed dependency list before inspecting the actual effect imports.

Native descriptor/event mapping or relevant player entity/component resource if needed to resolve which startup/loop/exit resources are selected. Exact entity path is not established by the available script/config sources.
Game build and source archive metadata/hashes so private clone comparison can demonstrate only intended color payload/track changes.
limits: No original vanilla binary .effect, particle, material, LUT or player entity was obtained by this trace.
No full original visual track list can be certified from public script/Tweak sources alone.
No REDscript compile, game resource load, native dispatch cache behavior, shader output or GPU rendering validated.
